case_name: Keith Thaete, Steve King, Lance Thaete v. St. Luke's Magic Valley Center, Michael R. Fry, D.O

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction: service of notice
issues.why: The court must decide whether failure to serve the notice of appeal deprives it of appellate jurisdiction or is a curable defect under the applicable rules.

issues.label: Timeliness of notice of appeal
issues.why: The court must confirm the appeal was filed within the time permitted after entry of final judgment.

issues.label: Appealability/finality of orders
issues.why: The court must determine whether the challenged rulings are encompassed in an appeal from a final judgment and properly before the court.

issues.label: Preservation of issues
issues.why: The court must decide whether each argument was raised below (including in reconsideration) to be reviewable on appeal.

issues.label: Standard of review: summary judgment
issues.why: The court must apply de novo review to whether any genuine dispute of material fact exists and whether respondents are entitled to judgment as a matter of law.

issues.label: Standard of review: expert admissibility
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard to evidentiary rulings that exclude expert testimony, distinct from summary-judgment standards.

issues.label: Standard of review: motion to strike
issues.why: The court must review the strike order for abuse of discretion under the Lunneborg framework.

issues.label: Lunneborg step: discretion recognized
issues.why: The court must determine whether the trial court recognized the issue as discretionary.

issues.label: Lunneborg step: correct standard
issues.why: The court must determine whether the trial court acted within legal standards governing late filings, rebuttal evidence, and expert disclosure.

issues.label: Lunneborg step: reasoned decision
issues.why: The court must determine whether the trial court reached its decision by an exercise of reason.

issues.label: Lunneborg step: applicable factors
issues.why: The court must determine whether relevant factors (prejudice, notice, cure, justification, docket) were considered and irrelevant ones avoided.

issues.label: Authority to modify response deadline
issues.why: The court must determine whether the court’s order extending the response deadline to August 22 governed and what filings were authorized thereafter.

issues.label: Untimeliness of Aug 28/29 filings
issues.why: The court must decide whether the rebuttal declarations and supplemental response were late under the court’s order and rules.

issues.label: Excusable neglect/good cause
issues.why: If late, the court must decide whether the Thaetes showed good cause or excusable neglect to permit the filings.

issues.label: Sanction proportionality
issues.why: The court must consider whether striking evidence was a proportionate remedy versus lesser measures (continuance, costs, limited supplementation).

issues.label: Prejudice to respondents
issues.why: The court must assess whether the late filings unfairly prejudiced respondents’ ability to respond to summary judgment or prepare for trial.

issues.label: Cure/continuance feasibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether any prejudice could have been cured without striking (e.g., allowing sur-reply, reopening depositions).

issues.label: Rebuttal vs case-in-chief evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the declarations were proper rebuttal or impermissibly supplied missing elements of plaintiffs’ prima facie case.

issues.label: New opinions in late declarations
issues.why: The court must determine whether the late filings introduced new standard-of-care/breach theories beyond timely disclosures.

issues.label: Rule governing summary-judgment evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether the declarations complied with requirements for affidavits/declarations (personal knowledge, admissible facts, competency).

issues.label: Admissibility decided before material fact
issues.why: The court must ensure it assessed admissibility of expert opinions as a threshold matter before deciding if a genuine dispute exists.

issues.label: Idaho MMA elements
issues.why: The court must identify the required elements—standard of care, breach, and proximate causation—under Idaho’s Medical Malpractice Act.

issues.label: Need for expert testimony
issues.why: The court must decide whether expert testimony is required on standard of care/breach/causation or whether any exception applies.

issues.label: Common-knowledge exception
issues.why: The court must decide whether the contraindicated-drug prescribing error is within common knowledge such that expert proof is unnecessary.

issues.label: Res ipsa considerations
issues.why: The court must consider whether any res ipsa-type inference is available in medical malpractice under Idaho law for the event described.

issues.label: Community standard foundation
issues.why: The court must decide whether each standard-of-care expert demonstrated actual knowledge of the applicable community standard under I.C. 6-1012.

issues.label: Similar community requirement
issues.why: The court must determine what “community” applies (Twin Falls or similar) and whether the experts tied opinions to that community or similar ones.

issues.label: Foundation under I.C. 6-1013
issues.why: The court must decide whether the experts adequately established how they learned the local standard (practice, inquiry, study, consultation, etc.).

issues.label: Board certification relevance
issues.why: The court must decide what weight shared board certification has in establishing familiarity with the applicable standard of care.

issues.label: Dr. McIlraith competency
issues.why: The court must decide whether Dr. McIlraith was qualified and had sufficient foundational basis to opine on Dr. Fry’s standard of care and breach.

issues.label: Dr. McIlraith preparation details
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record showed adequate inquiry/preparation (e.g., consultation with local providers, review of local practices) to meet 6-1012/1013.

issues.label: Precision of Dr. Fry deposition
issues.why: The court must decide whether ambiguity in Dr. Fry’s deposition affected the foundation analysis or created factual disputes on standard of care.

issues.label: Causation opinion necessity
issues.why: The court must decide whether admissible expert testimony is required to link Paxil+Nardil administration to death and whether such testimony was timely disclosed.

issues.label: Proximate cause standard
issues.why: The court must determine the correct legal causation standard (more likely than not) and whether evidence meets it.

issues.label: Apportionment/multiple actors
issues.why: The court must consider whether causation and fault must be analyzed among physician, nurses, and hospital policies or systems.

issues.label: Nurse Chisum disclosure sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether Nurse Chisum was disclosed with an opinion that nursing staff breached the standard of care and whether that disclosure met rule requirements.

issues.label: Nurse Chisum willingness to testify
issues.why: The court must decide whether counsel’s representations about unwillingness affect admissibility, availability, or whether the court properly relied on them.

issues.label: Effect of missing Chisum declaration
issues.why: The court must determine whether the absence of a timely supporting declaration justified exclusion at summary judgment.

issues.label: Nurse expert scope limits
issues.why: The court must determine whether nursing experts can opine on physician standard of care, hospital standard of care, medication reconciliation, and causation within their competencies.

issues.label: Nurse Tripp disclosure timeliness
issues.why: The court must decide whether the June supplemental disclosure violated the amended scheduling order and, if so, the appropriate consequence.

issues.label: Good cause for late witness
issues.why: If untimely, the court must decide whether there was good cause or harmlessness to allow Nurse Tripp despite the scheduling order.

issues.label: Scheduling order enforcement
issues.why: The court must decide the extent of the trial court’s discretion to enforce expert deadlines versus deciding cases on the merits.

issues.label: Hospital liability theory clarity
issues.why: The court must determine the precise theory against St. Luke’s (vicarious liability for staff, direct negligence/policies, medication reconciliation systems) and what expert proof is required.

issues.label: Vicarious liability prerequisites
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record supports that alleged negligent actors were agents/employees of St. Luke’s acting within scope.

issues.label: Direct corporate negligence
issues.why: The court must decide whether a claim based on hospital policies/practices requires separate standard-of-care evidence and was properly supported.

issues.label: Medication reconciliation duty
issues.why: The court must decide whether the applicable standard required obtaining, documenting, and acting on home-medication information (Nardil) and by whom.

issues.label: Conflicting evidence about notice
issues.why: The court must determine whether disputes over whether Dr. Fry/nurses saw the prescription bottles create genuine issues of material fact on breach/knowledge.

issues.label: Constructive notice
issues.why: The court must decide whether knowledge of Nardil can be imputed to Dr. Fry or St. Luke’s through staff or records even if he denies actual knowledge.

issues.label: Charting/computer entry significance
issues.why: The court must consider whether failure to enter home meds into the system is itself a breach and how it bears on causation.

issues.label: Contraindication standard of care
issues.why: The court must determine the standard governing prescribing SSRIs with MAOIs and required checking of medication lists, interactions, and psychiatric history.

issues.label: Reckless conduct label effect
issues.why: The court must decide whether “reckless conduct” alters elements, burdens, or available damages within the MMA framework.

issues.label: Negligence per se viability
issues.why: The court must decide whether any statute/regulation was identified that can support negligence per se in a medical malpractice action.

issues.label: Wrongful death standing/damages
issues.why: Because Sherry Thaete is deceased, the court must ensure proper statutory basis for wrongful death/survival claims, parties, and recoverable damages.

issues.label: Effect of Sherry’s death on parties
issues.why: The court must determine whether the proper estate/personal representative is required and whether the pleadings satisfy that requirement.

issues.label: Comparative fault defenses
issues.why: The court must consider whether any comparative fault issues (e.g., medication information provided, patient history) are legally relevant or supported.

issues.label: Summary-judgment burden shifting
issues.why: The court must decide whether respondents met their initial burden and whether plaintiffs then produced admissible evidence creating a triable issue.

issues.label: Use of discovery materials
issues.why: The court must decide what deposition testimony, disclosures, and produced policies can be considered at summary judgment and for what purposes.

issues.label: Hospital policy relevance/admissibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether internal policies are admissible as evidence of the standard of care or only as some evidence of negligence.

issues.label: Policy production timing impact
issues.why: The court must consider whether late production of policies affected plaintiffs’ ability to timely disclose opinions and whether relief was warranted.

issues.label: Meet-and-confer/compel history impact
issues.why: The court must assess whether prior discovery disputes bear on diligence, good cause, or fairness in enforcing disclosure deadlines.

issues.label: Reconsideration standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard for reconsideration and decide whether new arguments/evidence were properly considered or barred.

issues.label: Scope of reconsideration record
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs could cure summary-judgment deficiencies on reconsideration with evidence not timely presented.

issues.label: Attorney fees entitlement
issues.why: The court must determine whether either side is entitled to fees under Idaho statutes/rules (e.g., frivolous appeal, prevailing party, discretionary fees).

issues.label: Costs on appeal
issues.why: The court must decide which party is the prevailing party for purposes of awarding costs.

issues.label: Remedy if error found
issues.why: The court must decide whether to reverse and remand for trial, remand for further expert admissibility findings, or reinstate evidence with conditions.
